newsitem.title: UK: BT says grows despite fierce competition.
newsitem.headline: BT says grows despite fierce competition.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc, the country's dominant telephone giant, said on Thursday that it was succeeding in growing within its domestic market despite increased competition and price cuts.

"Demand for our advanced products and services remains strong and we continue to keep costs under control," said BT's chairman Sir Iain Vallance in the results statement. BT earlier reported profits for the year to March 31, 1997 had risen to 3.2 billion pounds ($5.3 billion) from a previous 3.0 billion.
Inland telephone call turnover was virtually unchanged in the year at 4.874 billion stg with volume growth of seven percent matched by the impact of price cuts which were worth seven percent overall.

BT, which hopes to win U.S. regulatory clearance for its $20 billion merger with American carrier MCI Communications Corp around autumn, said the new group would be uniquely placed to meet the opportunities for the fast liberalising global markets.
Group turnover at 14.935 billion pounds rose 3.4 percent with overall growth for products up eight percent, the company said.
"This growth was attributable to BT's expanding overseas operations, exchange line rentals, advanced services, mobile communications and private circuits," the group stated.

Growth in BT's overseas operations was mainly atrtributed to the success of its Dutch operations bought last April and that of its Concert communications services in continental Europe, North America and the rest of the world -- which it operates with MCI.
Price cuts in the year amounted to more than 800 million pounds -- nearly six percent of turnover, BT said.

International telephone call turnover fell in the face of fierce price cuts and a strengthening sterling. International call prices were cut by 14 percent in the year. Together with the impact of the strength of sterling in the second half of the year, international telephone turnover fell 8.6 percent.
Annual volume growth was seven percent
Because the fourth quarter had fewer working days than the same period in 1996, turnover was hit by more than 60 million pounds, BT said.
But mobile communications saw turnover rise 10.9 percent to 949 million pounds.
Bt's majority-owned cellular subsidiary Cellnet saw subscribers rise by 12.9 percent to 2.7 million connections of which 1.1. million were digital.

BT is paying a final dividend of 11.95 pence, making a 6.1 percent increae in total dividend to 19.85 pence. In addition, it proposes to pay a special dividend of 35 pence per share, costing 2.24 billion pounds
